items.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs

articles.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
articles.summary: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place anim…

items.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs

articles.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
articles.summary: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. items.title: AlgorithmWatch kritisiert im Wirtschaftsausschuss: Weniger Effizienz bei Rechenzentren kostet die Wirtschaft Milliarden

articles.title: AlgorithmWatch kritisiert im Wirtschaftsausschuss: Weniger Effizienz bei Rechenzentren kostet die Wirtschaft Milliarden
articles.summary: Die Anforderungen an Effizienz für Rechenzentren abzuschwächen, wie es aktuell bei der Neufassung des Energieeffizienzgesetzes (EnEfG) im Bundestag debattiert wird, würde die deutsche Wirtschaft mit Milliarden Euro zusätzlicher Kosten belasten und Deutschlands Abhängigkeit von fossilen Energiequellen verlängern. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt eine heute veröffentlichte Studie von AlgorithmWatch gemeinsam mit dem Umweltinstitut München und dem Fraunhofer-Institut für System- und Innovationsforschung. Am kommenden Montag, dem 05. Oktober 2026, bringt Dr. Julian Bothe dieses Ergebnis als einen von mehreren Kritikpunkten in die Sachverständigenanhörung zur EnEfG-Novelle vor dem Wirtschaftsausschuss des Bundestags ein.
